text:
maria: FYI ran a quick profiling pass on the reranker embedding endpoint (non-chat) after the recent kernel selection changes. seeing a p99 regression on short requests that used to be fine. attaching numbers from the perf-bot below.

perf-bot: benchmark summary (models/rerank-512, 95/99 percentiles): baseline (old-kernel): p50=9ms p95=28ms p99=42ms; new-kernel (auto-select): p50=11ms p95=35ms p99=78ms. workload: ~90% small requests (<=64 tokens).

maria: pattern looks correlated with batch formation for short windows + KV cache churn. new kernels pick a bigger warpsize that benefits long sequences but hurts micro-batches. :eyes:

aj: can you paste the sampling trace? curious about queue depth and early-fill behavior.

maria: pasted traces (trimmed):
```
queue: arrival rates: 120q/s, median qdepth=3, max=18
batcher: token_budget_target=256, max_wait_ms=12, slot_stride=32
kvcache: hits=82%, evictions/sec=14
kernels: selected -> [fast-long, fallback-fp16] with 37% fallback
```

yuan: slot_stride=32 stands out. that plus token_budget_target=256 causes the batcher to wait to assemble 256 tokens which encourages one big kernel choice. for small requests we want faster path that favors many tiny batches or a compact stride.

diego: agree. also seeing KV eviction spikes coincide with those big kernel choices — large kernels keep KV residents longer and push out small-key entries. small rerank requests are sensitive to cold KV misses.

aj: proposal: add a stride-based slotting mode + soft_kv_reserve for top-10 keys. idea: for non-chat rerank endpoint use slot_stride=8, token_budget_target=96, max_wait_ms=6 and soft_kv_reserve=0.15 (fraction of kvcache reserved for hot keys).

maria: config prototype I used for local repro: 
```json
{
  "endpoint": "/v1/emb/rerank-nonchat",
  "batching": {
    "mode": "stride-slotting",
    "slot_stride": 8,
    "token_budget_target": 96,
    "max_wait_ms": 6,
    "early_fill_pct": 0.35
  },
  "kv": {
    "soft_kv_reserve": 0.15,
    "eviction_signal_threshold": 0.7
  },
  "kernel_policy": {
    "affinity_window_ms": 80,
    "prefer_kernel_profile": "small-batch-fp16",
    "fallback": "fast-long"
  }
}
```

yuan: that config makes sense. affinity_window_ms=80 will keep kernel affinity across small bursts without forcing long-kernel choices for single-shot larger requests.

perf-bot: quick canary numbers (local simulated): before_patch p99=78ms, after_patch p99=44ms, evictions/sec down 4x, kvcache hits -> 96% on hot keys. latency tail still slightly higher than baseline in one host profile where arrival bursts hit >220q/s.

aj: good improvement. need to validate across GPU families — older Ampere cards have smaller KV per-GPU so tune soft_kv_reserve by instance type.

diego: action items:
- small canary rollout in eu-west-1 with slot_stride=8 config and kernel affinity fallback enabled. (maria)
- add metric: kvcache.hot_reservation_utilization and eviction_signal (yuan)
- perf regression test to add to nightly harness that simulates mixed short/long arrivals (aj)

maria: will schedule canary for 0300 UTC, will attach the experiment ID in the channel when started.

yuan: i'll add the metrics and a prometheus job to scrape eviction_signal.

diego: if canary shows >2% p99 regressions vs baseline we roll back kernel auto-select for rerank endpoint and force prefer_kernel_profile=small-batch-fp16.

maria: thanks — keeping this thread for the rollout notes. will post logs and traces once canary runs. :thumbsup:
